declarations.docstring: An auxiliary type depending on a field and a natural number.
An auxiliary family of types indexed by the elements of a finite type.
The additive commutative group structure on a finite-index auxiliary type.
The scalar-module structure over the ground field on a finite-index auxiliary type.
The module structure over the auxiliary matrix subalgebra on a finite-index auxiliary type.
Each finite-index auxiliary type is nontrivial.
Scalar multiplication by an element of the auxiliary matrix subalgebra is multiplication by its corresponding diagonal entry.
An auxiliary element of the matrix subalgebra associated with a finite index.
The commutator of an indexed auxiliary element with an element of the auxiliary matrix subalgebra belongs to the auxiliary ideal.
The underlying matrix of an indexed auxiliary element is the corresponding diagonal single-entry matrix.
An auxiliary algebra homomorphism from the matrix subalgebra to the ground field, associated with a finite index.
The indexed auxiliary algebra homomorphism evaluates an element at the corresponding diagonal position.
Applying an indexed auxiliary algebra homomorphism to an indexed auxiliary element gives one at matching indices and zero otherwise.
Each indexed auxiliary algebra homomorphism is surjective.
Every simple module over the auxiliary matrix subalgebra is linearly equivalent to a finite-index auxiliary type at some index.
For a positive natural-number parameter, the corresponding field-indexed auxiliary type has dimension one over the ground field.
Every finite-index auxiliary type has dimension one over the ground field.
For a positive exponent, the ideal generated by the adjoined root of X raised to that exponent is maximal.
For a positive exponent, the field-and-natural-number auxiliary type is simple over the corresponding adjoin-root algebra.
Each finite-index auxiliary type is simple over the auxiliary matrix subalgebra.
The kernel of the auxiliary algebra homomorphism from the adjoin-root algebra is the ideal generated by the adjoined root.
Right multiplication of a matrix by a diagonal matrix unit retains the indexed column and vanishes on all other columns.
For a positive exponent, every simple module over the corresponding adjoin-root algebra is linearly equivalent to the field-and-natural-number auxiliary type.
Finite-index auxiliary types at distinct indices are not linearly equivalent over the auxiliary matrix subalgebra.
For a positive exponent, the Jacobson radical of the corresponding adjoin-root algebra is the ideal generated by its adjoined root.
The Jacobson radical of the auxiliary matrix subalgebra is the auxiliary ideal.
The adjoined root acts as zero on the field-and-natural-number auxiliary type.
Left multiplication of a matrix by a diagonal matrix unit retains the indexed row and vanishes on all other rows.
An auxiliary ideal of the auxiliary matrix subalgebra.
The auxiliary ideal is two-sided.
Every element of the auxiliary ideal acts as zero on every simple module over the auxiliary matrix subalgebra.
The product of the difference between an algebra element and the scalar obtained from its indexed auxiliary homomorphism with the associated indexed auxiliary element belongs to the auxiliary ideal.
The sum of all indexed auxiliary elements in the matrix subalgebra is one.
For a positive exponent, an auxiliary algebra homomorphism from the corresponding adjoin-root algebra to the ground field.
The auxiliary adjoin-root algebra homomorphism applied to the image of a polynomial equals that polynomial evaluated at zero.
The auxiliary adjoin-root algebra homomorphism sends the adjoined root to zero.
The auxiliary adjoin-root algebra homomorphism is surjective.
For a positive exponent, the field-and-natural-number auxiliary type is algebra-equivalent to the ground field.
An auxiliary subalgebra of square matrices over a field, parameterized by their finite index size.
